To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) people who are high in prejudice toward homosexuals perceive research consistent with their attitudes as more convincing than disconfirming research, and (b) this biased assimilation process is mediated by negative affective reactions.

biased assimilation and polarization of attitude were observed when individuals with moderate attitudes read information that was consistent or inconsistent with their attitudes, and that negative affect mediated these biased processes.
biased assimilation and polarization occurred in the processing of scientific information about homosexuals and that affect mediated biased processing.

the role of affect as a moderator of the processing and effects of stereotype-relevant information.
